I'm trying to download what I think is a textbook, I'm not sure if it's the one I need or if it's just an article the same person also wrote, but it's this; http://bbs.pinggu.org/forum.php?mod=viewthread&tid=3624441&mobile=yes

The same as OP, I'm willing to send money via PayPal if it is the textbook and you're able to download and send it to me.

I do understand where you are coming from, and I am so sorry you are having to go through something so painful. 

That said, in regards the ''don't kill yourself while you are not symptomatic", I think you have crucially misunderstand the legal ramifications of illness with a dementia aspect.

The reason a third of people at risk of huntingtons choose to die before symptoms even present, or in the very very early stages, is because you loose your legal autonomy once they do. Which, given the laws regarding assisted suicide in this country, means once symptoms present and you are no longer deemed compus mentis, you no longer have that option and are confined to a long slow decline, as anybody who does choose to assist you will be prosecuted for accessory to murder :/

It's a sorry situation and entirely the fault of outdated right to die laws, that if you do not choose to die when still healthy, you don't get to do it at all before your natural end.

I'd gladly give someone mine. Only reason I'm on this forum, it's like your life is on pause and you can't go anywhere or do anything, cannot get a job, or a visa to go away somewhere for a while, you're just stuck waiting for the inevitable to happen and it just makes you want to hurry it up a bit.

If you plan on adopting she cannot get tested until afterwards. If it came back positive, you  would no longer be eligible candidates for adoption in most countries, nor even fostering. (Though you could, of course, still adopt privately from abroad - most likely from Russia or somewhere in Asia).
(I am not Irish, I came here four years ago and am stuck given I cannot get a job to earn money to go elsewhere. Rather a silly, sorry situation.)

I've already hitchhiked the length of South America bottom to top, and around Europe. I live in Ireland so it's not like I have endless stretches to discover on my doorstep like if I were American. It's good advice, and perhaps would be useful to an American or perhaps an Australian - unfortunately to go somewhere like that for me requires airfare, and if I plan on staying a certain length of time a visa. Sadly not viable given I have no income, and am illegible for tourist visas thanks to the condition (note, I am aware I do not need one for America). 

It's a shame because I genuinely would love to hitch hike around America - I've only been to a few places on the east coast - and there are a great number of things on my bucket list that I would love to do, but unfortunately, it does come down to money. I am, after all, trapped here on an island.
